task.title: Check the Host name, not just the port, when the board is bound off loopback
task.description:
Deferred minor from the adversarial review of PR #27 (WB-01KZBT0R3KS9DCFGSRP2J7C22X, branch fix/web-origin-host-guard).

internal/webui/guard.go:105 decides the Host check with:

    if !ok || port != guard.port || (guard.loopback && !loopbackHost(host))

When the listener is not bound to a loopback address, guard.loopback is false and the host name is never examined — only the port is. So on `workbook serve --addr 0.0.0.0:7331` (or a LAN IP) an attacker who rebinds evil.example to the victim's LAN address can have the victim's browser fetch http://evil.example:7331/api/tasks: the port matches, the name is unchecked, and because the browser now considers that target same-origin with the attacker page it sends no Origin header, so the Origin check is skipped as well. A follow-up POST with Content-Type: application/json passes all three checks and creates a task that boardPublisher pushes to origin. Reviewer reproduced this by extracting newOriginGuard/reject verbatim into a scratch module: reject(bound="0.0.0.0:7331", Host="evil.example:7331") returns 0 (allowed) for both the GET and the JSON POST, and likewise for bound="192.168.1.5:7331".

Two documentation problems travel with it. README.md:663 says flatly "The `Host` header must name the address the listener bound", which is not what happens in this mode — only the following sentence, which is scoped to loopback, is accurate. The exposure warning at internal/cli/run.go:900 says only that the board is "reachable beyond this machine" and does not say that any page on the internet can drive it through DNS rebinding. AGENTS.md requires the README to match implemented behavior and to distinguish guarantees from best-effort.

Candidate fixes: compare Host against the configured --addr host whenever that host is not a wildcard; or, on a wildcard bind, require Host to be an IP literal, since rebinding requires a name. Then say in the README exactly which mode gets which guarantee, and widen the serve warning.

Why deferred from PR #27: the ticket's acceptance criterion is worded as "not the bound loopback host and port", so loopback — the documented and default deployment — is fully covered by what shipped, and this is a weakening only in the already-warned exposed mode. The current behavior is deliberate and pinned by TestGuardOnNonLoopbackBindChecksPortAndSelfOrigin (internal/webui/guard_test.go:248), so changing it is a contract change with its own test rewrite rather than a fix to land under review.
